gloss: twists and turns; complications; ups and downs

definitions.explanation: A complicated process with many changes, setbacks, and difficulties along the way.

examples.japanese: {紆余曲折|うよきょくせつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{経|へ}て→経る：13876_heru⟧⟦ようやく→ようやく：00429_youyaku⟧⟦{完成|かんせい}した→完成する：01550_kansei⟧。
examples.english: After many twists and turns, it was finally completed.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}ら→彼ら：01802_karera⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{紆余曲折|うよきょくせつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Their relationship had its ups and downs.

examples.japanese: {紆余曲折|うよきょくせつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{末|すえ}→末：03362_sue⟧、⟦{契約|けいやく}→契約：02698_keiyaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{成立|せいりつ}した→成立する：04353_seiritsu⟧。
examples.english: After many complications, the contract was finalized.

examples.japanese: {紆余曲折|うよきょくせつ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{最終的|さいしゅうてき}→最終的：13013_saishuuteki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦うまくいった→うまくいく：21787_umakuiku⟧。
examples.english: There were twists and turns, but in the end things worked out.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}ち{上|あ}げる→立ち上げる：07892_tachiageru⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦さまざまな→さまざま：01559_samazama⟧{紆余曲折|うよきょくせつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{経験|けいけん}した→経験する：01179_keiken⟧。
examples.english: I went through various twists and turns before starting the company.

notes:
WORD FORMATION (YOJIJUKUGO):
⟦{紆余|うよ}→紆余：20891_uyo⟧ (winding) + ⟦{曲折|きょくせつ}→曲折：16399_kyokusetsu⟧ (bends and turns)
→ winding and bending = twists and turns

KANJI BREAKDOWN:
・{紆|う} - winding, meandering
・{余|よ} - surplus, extra
・{曲|きょく} - bend, curve
・{折|せつ} - break, fold

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{紆余曲折|うよきょくせつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{経|へ}て→経る：13876_heru⟧ - after many twists and turns
・{紆余曲折|うよきょくせつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{末|すえ}→末：03362_sue⟧ - after various complications
・{紆余曲折|うよきょくせつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧ - to have complications

NUANCE:
Emphasizes that the route to a result was anything but straightforward. It is most often used looking back, once the goal has finally been reached, so it carries a note of relief rather than complaint. The word is written and somewhat formal: it is at home in speeches, news writing, and business reports, and sounds heavy in casual chat.

GRAMMAR:
A noun, not a na-adjective - it does not take な. It appears as the object of ⟦{経|へ}る→経る：13876_heru⟧, as the subject of ⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧, or before ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{末|すえ}→末：03362_sue⟧.
